pairs.difference: A (popcorn cart): soft, slightly blurred surfaces. The popcorn and red cart body are smooth and the glass has one broad soft streak, which matches the real-card softness. B (station clock): crisp hard edges everywhere, with a dense ring of sharp minute dots, hard-edged hands and an evenly lacquered grey metal rim. Detail, micro-texture and gloss all sit above the real range.
pairs.fix: Soften the clock: draw the rim as matte brushed grey with one soft highlight, make the minute dots fewer and softer-edged, and let the edges blur slightly as on the real cards.

pairs.difference: A (spring duck): soft yellow plastic with broad, gentle highlights and a slightly blurred, quiet surface, like the real cards. B (cactus): an evenly glossy green skin with crisp specular streaks down every rib and sharp, shiny yellow spines repeated over the whole body. Gloss share is 0.173, above the real range.
pairs.fix: Make the cactus skin matte and waxy with only a faint soft sheen on the ribs. Use fewer, smaller, softer spines that are not shiny.

pairs.difference: A (saddle): every part is the same smooth, satin, plastic-like brown, with no stitching along the skirt or fender and no leather grain. The flap edges are rounded like moulded toy plastic, and only the metal rings read as a different material. B (fountain): matte sandstone with soft carved lobes and quiet paving, plus translucent water. It sits within the real look. The evidence is weak because the real cards are also smooth.
pairs.fix: Show the saddle as leather: a faint stitch line along the skirt and fender edges, a slightly matte seat with one soft sheen, and darker worn edges. Keep the rings bright metal.

pairs.difference: A (sneakers): the fine perforated mesh on the toe box and the glossy laces are busy, but they match the real-card range at its upper end. B (horseshoe): the metal reads as matte grey clay, with no metallic contrast, a soft smeared highlight along the inner curve and slightly mushy nail holes. The wood plank has decorative grain. Gloss share is 0.025, below the real range.
pairs.fix: Draw the horseshoe as worn iron: darker grey with a sharp, narrow bright highlight along the top edge, slightly pitted flat faces and crisp nail holes.

pairs.difference: A (sheriff star): a crisp, faceted red gem and hard-edged gold balls. The gold is a uniform saturated yellow plastic with no metallic contrast, and the edges are sharper than the real cards. B (umbrella): very soft and blurred, matte fabric panels, and a plain pole with no gloss. It is quiet like the real cards.
pairs.fix: Make the star read as metal: deeper gold with darker reflected tones and one sharp narrow highlight per arm, a slightly softer gem, and less uniform yellow.

pairs.difference: A (covered wagon): dense fine detail on the hero, with wrinkled canvas, many brass rivets, chain hooks, plank seams with grain on every board and glossy red rims. Detail, micro-texture and gloss are all at or above the top of the real range. B (rowboat): plank lines and a rope twist, but broad smooth surfaces and low gloss, which fits the real cards.
pairs.fix: Simplify the wagon surface: smooth canvas with two or three soft folds, a few rivets instead of a dense row, quiet wood with no visible grain, and matte wheel rims.

pairs.difference: A (flip-flops): smooth matte rubber soles with a simple dot tread and a glossy strap, and a low detail count like the real cards. B (cowboy boots): stitched decorative tooling on the shafts, a heel stack, a toothed spur and fine leather sheen. Detail and micro-texture are at the top of the real range.
pairs.fix: Reduce the boot detail: drop the tooled swirl stitching, or make it a faint tone-on-tone line, and use plain smooth leather with one soft highlight and a simple spur.

pairs.difference: A (scout jacket): soft fabric folds, pocket seams and glossy badges, all within the real range. B (cowboy hat): the felt is one smooth, uniform suede-like surface with a faint fine noise grain, and the band is plastic-glossy red. The surface looks airbrushed rather than built from material cues.
pairs.fix: Draw the hat as felt: matte with no sheen, slightly darker dents on the crown, and a band made of leather or fabric with a small buckle, not glossy plastic.

pairs.difference: A (scroll): matte paper and a soft wax seal, with the gloss confined to the blue table. It sits in the real range. B (phone booth): an evenly lacquered red over the whole booth, crisp window mullions, and a sharp keypad and display. Gloss share is 0.188 and micro-texture 0.023, both above the real range.
pairs.fix: Paint the booth in matte red paint with a slight sheen only on the roof curve. Make the window bars and keypad softer and less sharp.

pairs.difference: A (dock): soft orange planks with a few cut lines, a smooth rope coil and a glossy ring buoy, which matches the real softness. B (saloon): fine vertical wood-grain streaks over every clapboard, scattered pebbles in the ground and crisp hinges. Detail is 0.076 and micro-texture 0.034, both above the real range.
pairs.fix: Smooth the saloon walls into broad planks with no visible grain, remove the scattered pebbles, and soften all edges.

pairs.difference: A (lasso): a uniform, evenly repeated rope twist over every coil and an even satin sheen over the whole rope. Gloss is 0.158, above the real range. B (lawn mower): smooth red plastic with soft highlights and matte tyres, like the real cards.
pairs.fix: Make the rope matte and fibrous: a softer, less regular twist, no sheen, and slightly fuzzy edges.

pairs.difference: A (campfire pot): cast iron with fine speckle and a soft rim highlight, plus matte wood poles. It is plausible. B (gas pump): chipped-paint weathering patches at the base, crisp counter digits, and glossy orange paint with a sharp chrome nozzle. The weathering is decorative surface detail that the real cards do not show.
pairs.fix: Remove the chipped-paint patches and use clean, slightly matte orange paint with a single soft highlight and simpler, softer gauges.

pattern: Generated cards show more surface activity than the real ones. They add fine detail across the whole hero (rivets, tooling, wood grain on every plank, pebbles, rope twist, mesh) and lacquer it evenly, so gloss and micro-texture run above the real range. The other tell runs the opposite way: plastic-looking materials where leather, felt or iron should be (the saddle, the hat, the horseshoe). Real cards are softer and slightly blurred, with broad quiet surfaces and gloss held to one or two spots.
